title: Leeds defender Pascal Struijk to miss Chelsea match with hip injury
content:
Leeds United centre-back Pascal Struijk is set to miss Tuesday’s trip to Chelsea due to a hip flexor problem.

Struijk, 26, reported the issue after Friday’s win over Nottingham Forest.

It means Daniel Farke will be forced into at least one change for Tuesday’s fixture, with Anton Stach also not returning from his own hip issue at Stamford Bridge. The German is expected to be back in contention for the Aston Villa match on February 21.

Dominic Calvert-Lewin has been dealing with illness, but Farke hopes to have everyone other than Struijk and Stach available on Tuesday. He was asked in Monday’s press conference about the condition of Calvert-Lewin and Ilia Gruev.

“Both seem to be available,” he said. “Dominic was struggling a little bit with illness, but I hope it’s not too bad and I hope he is available.

“In terms of knocks or muscle injuries, there’s nothing. Also, Ilia is tough. Bad news with Pascal Struijk, he will definitely miss his game.

“He got some problems, after the game, with his hip flexor and the turnaround is a bit too quick. Anton Stach will also be back, probably just for the Villa game. Apart from this, I hope to have everyone available.”

Struijk has started 22 of Leeds’ 25 Premier League matches this season. Jaka Bijol, who returned to the matchday squad last Friday after injury, is likely to be who Farke turns to in his back three in Struijk’s absence.
